title: How Lenny grew his newsletter to 500,000 subscribers: ten lessons on quality, consistency, and focus
summary: Lenny reflects on hitting 500,000 subscribers and distills ten lessons. Growth comes from consistently publishing high-quality, original, shareable work, not from design, branding, or growth strategy. He covers picking a topic by energy, spending more time per post, cutting words, and sustaining a cadence.

principles.text: Growth comes from quality and consistency; design, title, strategy and growth plans mostly don't matter.
principles.quote: There’s no trick to making something like this grow. Growth comes from publishing something valuable, that people want to share with their friends and colleagues, over and over and over.

principles.text: Define the concrete job you do for a specific audience, and do it better than anyone.
principles.quote: Who exactly is your audience? Think of a specific person—what would they find extremely interesting or useful?

principles.text: Pick a topic by following your energy and real-life experience; avoid niches so narrow you get bored.
principles.quote: Follow your energy. What topics give you energy to think about, write about, and talk about? What saps you of energy? Spend more on the former and less on the latter.

principles.text: Time invested in content itself beats time on branding, website or strategy; most content is mediocre so better wins.
principles.quote: If you can spend almost zero time working on anything that isn’t creating the content itself, you’ll have an advantage.

principles.text: Cut 30-50% of your words: shorten intros and get to the meat fast.
principles.quote: Cut every word that isn’t ~absolutely~ necessary. Make your intro 50% shorter. Get into the meat of your post as quickly as possible.

principles.text: Contribute something new via primary research, and choose a sustainable cadence you can keep for years.
principles.quote: Remember, quality + consistency = you win, and people don’t want more emails. They want better emails.
